patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Project and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than Trello's shape. Choose Trello only if your buying job matches “Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Workflow advantage: Microsoft Project leans work-management, resource-planning; Trello leans team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Microsoft Project and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo.; Trello is Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise) vs Trello (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Microsoft Project-leaning work-management, resource-planning, timeline-reporting vs Trello-leaning team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Trello — Limited planning depth vs Work OS.

Limitations — Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation; Trello: Limited planning depth vs Work OS; Premium needed for richer views.

Poor-fit cases: Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · Trello is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Limited planning depth vs Work OS · Avoid Microsoft Project if you actually need Trello's motion (Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
